physicalNotes: Radius 0.2466772 Jupiter radii from Lillo-Box et al. 2023 (2023A&A...669A.109L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...669A.109L/abstract): 17,635.4 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.0286318 Jupiter masses (Lillo-Box et al. 2023, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2023A&A...669A.109L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...669A.109L/abstract) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Lillo-Box et al. 2023 (2023A&A...669A.109L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname LILLO_BOX_ET_AL_2023): P 1.8237305 d
sources.shape: Lillo-Box et al. 2023 (2023A&A...669A.109L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname LILLO_BOX_ET_AL_2023): a/R* 8.47; Lillo-Box et al. 2023 (2023A&A...669A.109L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname LILLO_BOX_ET_AL_2023): inclination 86.75 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Lillo-Box et al. 2023 (2023A&A...669A.109L), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname LILLO_BOX_ET_AL_2023): transit mid-time 2459248.37709 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 3 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
